The home mountain of the Greek Gods is Mount Olympus.

To understand how search engines work, imagine the Internet as a massive, infinite library. In this analogy, each website is like a specific book on a shelf, and the individual web pages within that site are the pages inside that book. If you are looking for a specific piece of information, you wouldn't want to read every book in the library from cover to cover. Instead, you would use a library index (or catalog) to find the exact book and page that contains what you need. Search engines like Google act as this intelligent index, scanning the vast library of the Internet to help you locate the precise website and page that holds the answer to your query.
